description:
Ergonomic tax on every type-dispatching library function.

Type-annotated clause heads are fz's answer to Elixir's is_* guards and they work
statically AND dynamically -- verified dispatching integer/float/binary/atom/list on
values arriving through a mailbox as any. But :: binds only at top-level parameter
positions:

  fnp flatten([head :: [any] | rest], tail), ...
  => error[internal/post-resolution-leftover]: unsupported quoted pattern head '::'

so nested dispatch needs a helper hop:

  fnp flatten([head | rest], tail), do: prepend(head, flatten(rest, tail))
  fnp prepend(head :: [any], tail), do: flatten(head, tail)
  fnp prepend(head, tail), do: [head | tail]

That version runs natively and matches Elixir's List.flatten on all inputs, so this
is friction, not a blocker. But it multiplies helper fan-out across the whole port --
the same tax that multi-statement -> arm bodies already impose (fz-kdt.151).
title: Allow :: type annotation in nested pattern positions
